sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar continues that even in intellect there is a concept of consolation, and gives an example from the verses about the flood where the same reasoning changed from a cause for punishment to a cause for mercy, explaining that the change in intellect comes from a change in will.

translations.translation: And he continues in the maamar,
that even in intellect there is a matter of consolation.
And he brings an example for this from that which at first76
it is written, "And every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil etc."
(and therefore)
"I will blot out etc.",
and afterwards77
it is written, "For the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth," and
(therefore)
"I will not again continue to smite etc."
For that same reasoning that was initially the cause that obligated became the cause that acquits.
And he explains,
that the change in intellect comes from the aspect of will.
For when a change occurs in the will,
the intellect also changes.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason the will changes the intellect is that the intellect is always connected to the will, unlike the relationship between intellect and emotions where intellect is clothed within them, raising the question of how a non-clothing cause like will can affect the intellect after it has already been drawn forth.

translations.translation: And the reason for this
(that through the will the intellect changes)
is,
that the intellect is always connected
(even after it has already been drawn forth from the will)
to the will,
and therefore,
when a change occurs in the will, the intellect also changes.
And in the manner that was explained above regarding the matter of intellect and emotions.
And one must understand,
but will and intellect are two different matters,
for intellect is internal
[that which is sometimes explained that intellect is a level of encompassing,
the intention in this is that it is not in the level of inner feeling as much as the emotions78],
and its activity in the brain is in a manner of clothing,
to the extent that through much engagement in intellectual concepts, a change occurs in the brain, with grooves being added to it79,
and likewise regarding the activity of the intellect upon the emotions in the heart,
that which it affects in the emotions is by means of clothing itself within them.
But not so the will, which is encompassing, not in a manner of clothing.
For it is likewise regarding the activity of the will upon the intellect
[that through the will a change occurs in the intellect,
which is why they said80
"A person should always study in a place where his heart desires"]
that this is not in a manner of clothing but in a manner of cause.
And based on this, explanation is needed,
for seemingly regarding intellect and emotions,
since the intellect is clothed within the emotions,
therefore even after the emotions have been drawn forth from the intellect, they are dependent upon the intellect,
and when a change occurs in the intellect, the emotions also change.
But not so regarding will and intellect,
since the will is only a cause for the drawing forth and revelation of the intellect,
what is the connection of the intellect
(after it has already been drawn forth)
with the will,
to the extent that through a change in the will, the intellect will also change.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This is understood through the Tzemach Tzedek's explanation of the verse "All that Hashem desires He does," that although all actions come from the specific Sefiros, they are attributed to the will because the will is the essence of the inner powers, as illustrated by the analogy of human action where the will activates the powers.

translations.translation: And this)
And this will be understood by prefacing what the Tzemach Tzedek explains at length in Ohr HaTorah Parshat Nasso81
and in brief in his Sefer HaMitzvos, Mitzvas Binyan Mikdash82
on the verse83
"All that Hashem desires He does,"
that one must understand,
behold, the creations came into being from the ten Sefiros that are below Kesser,
and more particularly from the seven emotions,
and why does He attribute all actions to the will, which is Kesser.
And seemingly one could add,
that one cannot say that that which came into being from the ten Sefiros is the particulars of the creations, and what is said "All that Hashem desires He does"
(specifically "all")
refers to the totality of creation,
for even the totality of creation came into being from Chochmah,
as explained in many places84
on the verse85
"All of them with wisdom You made,"
for the division within the creations is from the aspect of Binah,
but not so the coming into being from the aspect of Chochmah, which is in totality
("all of them with wisdom"),
and what is the meaning of "All that Hashem desires He does," that creation is from the will.
And he explains this with a parable from human action86,
that although every action comes from a specific power,
nevertheless, that the powers act is through the will,
and without will,
there would be no action at all.
And like the movement of the hand and foot,
that although the movement itself comes from the power of movement in the hand,
nevertheless,
in order for the movement to occur,
it is specifically through the will,
and without the will, the hand would rest like a silent stone
(even though it has the power of movement within it).
And likewise in the Supernal Man,
that this flow from the ten Sefiros to vitalize the worlds is from the aspect of the will,
and therefore all actions are attributed to the will,
"All that Hashem desires He does."
And one could say,
that this attribution of all actions to the will,
even though the actions themselves are drawn from the ten Sefiros and the will is only so that the Sefiros will bestow,
is
(as implied in Ohr HaTorah there)
because that the activity of the inner powers is through the will is because the inner powers are only a radiance and illumination from the soul, and the will is from the essence of the soul.
And therefore the actions are attributed to the will,
even though they are drawn from the inner powers,
for the will is
(like)
the essence of them.
